0.long_answer: Joubert syndrome is primarily a neurological condition characterized by cerebellar anomalies that lead to a variety of motor and sensory deficits, including hypotonia (low muscle tone). One of the distinctive facial features observed in the syndrome is ptosis, or drooping of the upper eyelids. This drooping is generally attributed to dysfunction in the muscle responsible for elevating the upper eyelid—the levator palpebrae superioris muscle. When this muscle is weak or its function is impaired due to the neurological aspects of Joubert syndrome, the ability to properly lift the upper eyelid diminishes, leading to ptosis.
